source: NCERT Class VII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, History Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. The Mauryan Empire
points: The **Mauryan Empire** — India's first great empire — was founded by **Chandragupta Maurya** in **c. 321 BCE**, with its capital at **Pataliputra**.
**Chanakya (Kautilya)**, his adviser, is credited with the **Arthashastra**, a manual on statecraft and economy.
**Megasthenes**, a Greek ambassador, wrote the **Indica** describing Mauryan India.
Chandragupta was followed by **Bindusara**, then the great **Ashoka**.

sections.heading: 2. Ashoka and the Kalinga War
points: **Ashoka** (c. 268–232 BCE) fought the bloody **Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE)**.
Shocked by the death and suffering, Ashoka **gave up war of conquest** and embraced **dhamma** (a moral code of right conduct).
**Dhamma** stressed: **non-violence, respect for elders, tolerance of all religions, kindness to servants and animals, truthfulness**.
He appointed **dhamma mahamatras** (special officers) to spread these ideas.

sections.heading: 3. Ashoka's Edicts
points: Ashoka was the **first Indian ruler to inscribe messages to his people** — on **rocks and pillars** across the empire.
Written mostly in **Prakrit** in the **Brahmi** script (and Kharosthi/Greek/Aramaic on the frontiers).
The **Lion Capital** of the **Sarnath** pillar is India's **national emblem**; the **Ashoka Chakra** is on the national flag.

sections.heading: 4. Administration and Decline
points: A vast empire governed from **Pataliputra**, with **provincial centres** (e.g. Taxila, Ujjayini, Suvarnagiri, Tosali) under **princes**.
A large **army, spies and officials**; roads and communication linked the empire.
After Ashoka, the empire **weakened and broke up** (large size, weak successors, financial strain); it ended around **185 BCE**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Mauryan Empire founded by Chandragupta Maurya (c. 321 BCE); capital Pataliputra.
Chanakya/Kautilya = Arthashastra; Megasthenes = Indica.
Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE) transformed Ashoka → dhamma; dhamma mahamatras spread it.
Ashoka = first ruler to inscribe edicts (rock & pillar), mostly Prakrit in Brahmi.
Sarnath Lion Capital = national emblem; empire ended c. 185 BCE.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Arthashastra** is linked to **Chanakya (Kautilya)**; the **Indica** to **Megasthenes**.
The **Kalinga War** changed **Ashoka** — after it he pursued **dhamma**, not conquest.
Ashoka's edicts are mostly in **Prakrit** written in the **Brahmi** script.
The **Lion Capital of Sarnath** is the national emblem; the empire is **Mauryan** (not Gupta).
